notes: Open subset of the realistic O/D pairs (70 of 70). Realistic commute pairs from public data. LODES 2023 home-to-work flows (all jobs, both ends in the service area, 1-15 km straight line) are scaled by the home tract's share of workers who bike to work (ACS 2019-2023 5-year B08301, shrunk toward the county share with a 200-worker prior), then summed by zone pair (bench/points/sf-zones.json). The 70 busiest zone pairs each get one pair: the busiest ~1 km home and work cells of that zone pair, each end moved to the nearest named OSM place within 0.5 km when there is one. weight = the zone pair's estimated bike commutes over the pairs kept (sums to 1); share = percent of all estimated in-range bike commutes it stands for. The pairs cover 35.7% of them. Zone pairs whose shortest bicycle route is over 2x the straight line (bay crossings with no bridge that carries bikes; those commuters ride to BART or a ferry) are skipped: 5 of them, 2.1% of estimated bike commutes, listed in skipped_water. Commute trips only: no recreation, errands or school. Regenerate with build_sf.py in the research workspace.
attribution: Contains data from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), US Census LEHD LODES 8, 2023 and US Census ACS 2019-2023 5-year estimates (public domain).
weight_note: weight is relative: weights sum to 1 over the full pair set, so this subset sums to 1.0000.
